questions.questionText: The box of mangoes ____ on the table.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'box'; 'of mangoes' does not change it. Singular subject takes 'is'.
questions.shortcut: Ignore the phrase between subject and verb.

questions.questionText: Each of the students ____ a separate locker.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb: has.

questions.questionText: Neither of the two answers ____ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' used with 'of' is treated as singular: is.

questions.questionText: Ravi and Karthik ____ going to the match tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: are.

questions.questionText: Bread and butter ____ my usual breakfast.
questions.explanation: Two nouns forming one idea are treated as a single unit: Bread and butter is.
questions.shortcut: One idea joined by and = singular.

questions.questionText: Either the manager or his assistants ____ responsible for the error.
questions.explanation: With either...or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'assistants' (plural): are.

questions.questionText: Neither the players nor the coach ____ happy with the result.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'coach' (singular); the past context gives was.

questions.questionText: Mathematics ____ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -s, such as mathematics, are singular.

questions.questionText: The news about the strike ____ shocking.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and singular: was.

questions.questionText: The police ____ arrested the suspect last night.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural collective noun and takes a plural verb: have.

questions.questionText: Fifty rupees ____ too much for this pen.
questions.explanation: A sum of money treated as a single amount takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: The number of vacancies ____ increasing every year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: A number of candidates ____ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb: are.

questions.questionText: One of my cousins ____ in Dubai.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'one', singular, so 'lives'.
questions.shortcut: One of + plural noun = singular verb.

questions.questionText: The jury ____ divided in their opinions.
questions.explanation: When the members act individually, a collective noun takes a plural verb: were.

questions.questionText: The Lok Sabha ____ adjourned till Monday.
questions.explanation: The name of a single body such as the Lok Sabha is treated as singular, so the past singular 'was' is used.

questions.questionText: Where ____ my glasses?
questions.explanation: 'Glasses' (spectacles) is a plural noun: are.

questions.questionText: A pair of scissors ____ on the table.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'pair', which is singular: is.

questions.questionText: Everyone in the room ____ clapping.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular: was.

questions.questionText: The teacher, along with her students, ____ visiting the museum.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not make the subject plural; the subject 'teacher' is singular: is.
questions.shortcut: along with / as well as / with = ignore.

questions.questionText: My friend as well as my brothers ____ invited to the wedding.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the first subject 'friend' (singular) when 'as well as' is used: was.
questions.shortcut: A as well as B: agree with A.

questions.questionText: Not only the principal but also the teachers ____ present.
questions.explanation: With not only...but also, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'teachers': were.

questions.questionText: The poet and the painter ____ great friends.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: are.

questions.questionText: The secretary and treasurer ____ resigned.
questions.explanation: With one article before both nouns, both titles refer to one person, so the verb is singular: has.

questions.questionText: There ____ many reasons for his failure.
questions.explanation: In a 'there' sentence the verb agrees with the real subject 'reasons' (plural): are.
questions.shortcut: There is/are: check the noun after it.

questions.questionText: There ____ two books and a pen on the desk.
questions.explanation: In a 'there' sentence the verb agrees with the first noun that follows, 'two books' (plural): are.

questions.questionText: Two-thirds of the land ____ under cultivation.
questions.explanation: With fractions, agreement follows the noun after 'of'; 'land' is singular: is.

questions.questionText: Two-thirds of the apples ____ rotten.
questions.explanation: With fractions, agreement follows the noun after 'of'; 'apples' is plural: are.

questions.questionText: Who ____ the author of this novel?
questions.explanation: 'Who' asking about one person takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: The scholar and the poet ____ both attended the function.
questions.explanation: 'Both' together with two subjects joined by 'and' shows plural: have.

questions.questionText: It is I who ____ responsible for this decision.
questions.explanation: In a relative clause the verb agrees with the antecedent 'I': am.
questions.shortcut: who takes the person of its antecedent.

questions.questionText: Ten kilometres ____ a long distance to walk in an hour.
questions.explanation: A distance considered as one unit takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: The Arabian Nights ____ a collection of stories.
questions.explanation: The title of a single work is singular: is.

questions.questionText: Many a student ____ failed in this paper.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and singular verb: has.
